title: Manual Jira UI verification testing
description:
Perform manual end-to-end testing by creating and viewing Jira tickets
with all supported formatting elements to verify the fixes render
correctly in the Jira web UI.

## Why manual testing?
Unit tests verify our conversion logic in isolation, but the ultimate
consumer of the output is the Jira web UI (or Jira API → web rendering).
There can be discrepancies between what our converter produces and what
Jira actually renders. Manual testing catches these gaps.

## Test procedure

### 1. Build and install the fixed CLI
```bash
cd /data/projects/jira-cli
go build -o jira ./cmd/jira-cli/
# Or use GoReleaser if available
```

### 2. Create a test ticket with all formatting elements
Using the CLI, create a ticket on prplfoundationcloud.atlassian.net with
a description containing ALL of the following:

- **Tables with links in cells**: A table where at least one cell contains
  a markdown link [text](url)
- **Headings**: All 6 levels (h1 through h6)
- **Text effects**: Bold, italic, strikethrough, underline, inline code
- **Links**: Standard links, links with query parameters
- **Code blocks**: With and without language tags, containing special chars
- **Lists**: Ordered, unordered, nested 3 levels deep
- **Blockquotes**: With rich text inside
- **Typed panels**: {info}, {warning}, {note}, {tip}, {error}, {success}
  with content
- **Horizontal rule**: `---`

### 3. Verify in Jira web UI
Open the created ticket at:
  https://prplfoundationcloud.atlassian.net/browse/<TICKET-KEY>

Check each formatting element renders correctly:
- [ ] Tables: columns aligned, links clickable
- [ ] Headings: correct hierarchy
- [ ] Bold/italic/strike/underline: visually distinct
- [ ] Code blocks: monospace, language syntax highlighting (if supported)
- [ ] Links: clickable, correct URL
- [ ] Lists: properly indented, correct markers
- [ ] Blockquotes: visually quoted
- [ ] Panels: colored backgrounds matching type
- [ ] Horizontal rule: visible separator

### 4. Test the reverse direction
View the ticket using `jira issue view <KEY>` and verify the CLI output
renders the formatting correctly in the terminal.

## Files involved
No files modified — this is a verification-only task.

## Key considerations
- If any rendering is incorrect, file a NEW bead for the specific issue
  with the "discovered-from" dependency type
- Take screenshots of the Jira web UI for documentation
- Test on both Jira Cloud (prplfoundationcloud.atlassian.net) since that's
  the target environment
- The CLI's terminal output goes through ADF→MD rendering, which is a
  different path than MD→Wiki. Both paths need verification.

title: Tag v1.7.0-ynezz.3 and build release
description:
Tag the release as v1.7.0-ynezz.3, build via GoReleaser, and install the
new binary. This is the final step that delivers the formatting fixes to
users.

## Context
The repo (ankitpokhrel/jira-cli fork at ynezz/jira-cli) uses semantic
versioning with a fork suffix. The current installed version is
v1.7.0-ynezz.2. This release increments the patch-level fork version.

## Release steps

### 1. Ensure all work is committed and pushed
```bash
git status            # Must be clean
git log --oneline -5  # Review recent commits
```

### 2. Tag the release
```bash
git tag -a v1.7.0-ynezz.3 -m "Release v1.7.0-ynezz.3: formatting fixes

Changes in this release:
- Fix links inside wiki table cells being mangled by pipe splitting
- Fix typed panel regex accepting mismatched open/close tags
- Add underline mark rendering in ADF→MD translator
- Expand test coverage: +18 to +26 new test cases across wiki parser,
  markdown converter, and ADF renderer
- Code block escaping: investigated (see release notes for status)"
git push origin v1.7.0-ynezz.3
```

### 3. Build with GoReleaser (if configured)
```bash
goreleaser release --clean
# Or if GoReleaser is not configured:
go build -ldflags "-X github.com/ankitpokhrel/jira-cli/internal/version.Version=v1.7.0-ynezz.3" -o jira ./cmd/jira-cli/
```

### 4. Install
```bash
# Move binary to PATH or install via go install
cp jira /usr/local/bin/jira
# Or:
go install -ldflags "-X github.com/ankitpokhrel/jira-cli/internal/version.Version=v1.7.0-ynezz.3" ./cmd/jira-cli/
```

### 5. Verify installation
```bash
jira version  # Should show v1.7.0-ynezz.3
```

## Files involved
No source files modified. Git tag and build artifacts only.

## Key considerations
- Do NOT tag until ALL tests pass and manual verification is complete
- The version string is embedded via ldflags — check the exact import path
  for the version package (internal/version)
- If GoReleaser is not configured for this fork, a simple `go build` with
  ldflags is sufficient
- After tagging, the formatting-fixes branch can be merged back into
  ynezz/issue-attachments (or directly into main, depending on workflow)
- Update any downstream consumers that pin the version

## What's included in this release
- Bug 1: Links inside table cells (FIXED — confirmed bug, p0)
- Bug 2: Code block escaping (INVESTIGATED — status depends on findings)
- Bug 3: Typed panel regex mismatch (FIXED — confirmed bug, p1)
- Bug 4: Underline mark rendering (IMPLEMENTED — new feature, p1)
- 18-26 new test cases across three test files

title: Run full test suite with race detection
description:
Run the complete Go test suite with race detection enabled to verify that
all Phase 1 tests pass after Phase 2 fixes are applied, and that no
existing tests have regressed.

## What this verifies
This is the integration gate between "all code changes are done" and
"ready for manual testing / release". It catches:
  - Regressions in existing tests caused by Phase 2 changes
  - Race conditions in any concurrent code paths
  - Compilation errors across the entire project
  - Any test that was expected to fail (TDD) but wasn't updated after fix

## Commands to run

```bash
# Full test suite with race detection (the canonical command)
go test -race ./...

# If the above is too slow, run targeted suites first:
go test -race -v ./pkg/md/...        # Wiki→MD and MD→Wiki paths
go test -race -v ./pkg/adf/...       # ADF→MD rendering
go test -race ./internal/...         # Internal packages
go test -race ./cmd/...              # Command handlers
```

## Expected outcome
- ALL tests pass (exit code 0)
- No race conditions detected
- No compilation errors

## What to do if tests fail
1. Identify which test(s) failed and which Phase 2 change caused it
2. Go back to the relevant Phase 2 bead and fix the issue
3. Re-run the full suite
4. Do NOT proceed to manual testing or release with failing tests

## Files involved
No files modified — this is a verification-only task.

## Key considerations
- The -race flag adds significant overhead; expect 2-5x slower execution
- Some tests may be flaky if they depend on timing — run twice if a
  single test fails intermittently
- The go test cache may mask failures; use -count=1 to force re-execution
  if you suspect caching: `go test -race -count=1 ./...`

title: Fix reference link parsing inside bold markup
description:
Wiki->MD reference-link conversion fails when a Jira link is wrapped in bold markup.

## Reproduction
Input:
  `*[text|url]*`

Current output:
  `**[text|url]**`

Expected output:
  `**[text](url)**`

## Impact
- Links inside bold text are not converted to Markdown link syntax.
- The parser leaves `|`-style Jira link syntax inside bold wrappers.

## Notes
- This surfaced while adding edge-case tests in `bd-2rb`.
- Related test case currently fails in `TestParseReferenceLinks/link inside bold markup`.

## Suspected area
`pkg/md/jirawiki/parser.go` reference-link handling order/interaction with text-effect parsing.
close_reason: Reference links inside bold markup now convert correctly in Wiki→MD parser

comments.author: Petr Štetiar
comments.text:
Fix implemented in `pkg/md/jirawiki/parser.go`:
- Updated `handleTextEffects()` to run `convertReferenceLinks()` on the inner bold span before emitting `**...**`.

Why this works:
- `*[text|url]*` is tokenized as a text-effect token first, so reference-link conversion was previously skipped inside the bold span.
- Converting links inside the span ensures bold-wrapped Jira links become Markdown links.

Validation:
- `go test -v -run 'TestParseReferenceLinks/link_inside_bold_markup' ./pkg/md/jirawiki` => PASS
- `go test ./pkg/md/jirawiki ./pkg/md` => PASS

title: Add MD→Wiki conversion regression tests
description:
Add 7 targeted test cases to TestToJiraMD in pkg/md/md_test.go that
exercise the CommonMark → Jira wiki conversion path, focusing on tables
with links, horizontal rules, nested lists, combined mark nesting, all
heading levels, blockquote with rich text, and mismatched typed panel tags.

## Background & motivation
The MD→Wiki path flows through ToJiraMD() in pkg/md/md.go, which:
  1. Runs convertTypedPanels() to rewrite typed panels ({info},{warning},etc.)
  2. Feeds the result through blackfriday with the confluence renderer

The existing TestToJiraMD (line 9) covers a broad golden-string comparison
but lacks targeted cases for specific edge cases. The existing
TestConvertTypedPanels (line 111) covers panel conversion but does NOT test
the mismatched-tag case (Bug 3).

These tests establish the baseline for Bug 3 (typed panel regex) and provide
regression anchors for other rendering behaviors.

## Test cases to add (new focused cases in TestToJiraMD or a new test function)

1. **Markdown table containing links (header and body)**
   Input: `| Col1 | Col2 |\n|---|---|\n| [Link](url) | text |`
   Expected: Jira table with `||Col1||Col2||` header and `|[Link|url]|text|` body.
   Rationale: Validates that the confluence renderer correctly reverse-maps
   CommonMark links to Jira link syntax inside table cells.

2. **Horizontal rule**
   Input: `---`
   Expected: `----` (Jira wiki horizontal rule is four dashes)
   Rationale: The plan notes MD→Wiki supports hr, but we need a targeted test.

3. **Nested lists preserve depth**
   Input: `- item1\n  - subitem\n    - subsubitem`
   Expected: Jira wiki nested list with `*`, `**`, `***` markers.
   Rationale: Indentation-based nesting must map to Jira's marker-count nesting.

4. **Combined bold+italic+code mark nesting**
   Input: `` **bold _italic `code`_** ``
   Expected: Corresponding Jira wiki: `*bold _italic {{code}}_*`
   Rationale: Multiple overlapping marks should compose correctly.

5. **All heading levels (1-6)**
   Input: `# H1\n## H2\n### H3\n#### H4\n##### H5\n###### H6`
   Expected: `h1. H1\nh2. H2\nh3. H3\nh4. H4\nh5. H5\nh6. H6`
   Rationale: Ensures all 6 levels map correctly, not just the commonly used 1-3.

6. **Blockquote containing nested rich text**
   Input: `> **bold** and _italic_ in a quote`
   Expected: `{quote}*bold* and _italic_ in a quote{quote}`
   Rationale: Rich text inside blockquotes must be converted, not flattened.

7. **Mismatched typed panel tags left unchanged**
   Input: `{info}content{warning}`
   Expected: `{info}content{warning}` (NOT rewritten to {panel:bgColor=...})
   Rationale: This is the failing test for Bug 3. The current regex
   `typedPanelPattern` captures open/close types independently without
   requiring them to match, so `{info}x{warning}` would incorrectly be
   rewritten. This test must FAIL on current HEAD.

## File to modify
`pkg/md/md_test.go` — TestToJiraMD (starts at line 9) or add new test functions

## Key considerations
- Test #7 (mismatched panels) MUST fail on current HEAD — it's the TDD
  foundation for Bug 3
- Tests #1-6 may pass or fail depending on current renderer behavior;
  run each individually to determine status
- The blackfriday-confluence renderer is an external dependency — some
  behaviors may be renderer-level limitations rather than bugs in our code
- Do NOT gate code-block escaping tests on this task (that's a separate
  investigation with its own bead)
- Important: the plan says to "gate any code-block escaping test on a
  reproducible failing fixture from current HEAD"
close_reason: Completed: added targeted MD→Wiki regression tests; surfaced bugs in panel tag matching and nested list depth

title: Fix links inside Wiki→MD table cells (Bug 1)
description:
Fix the confirmed bug where Jira link syntax [text|url] inside table cells
is incorrectly split by the pipe character, producing garbled markdown tables
with wrong column counts.

## Root cause analysis
In pkg/md/jirawiki/parser.go, the handleTable() method (line 482) processes
table rows as follows:

1. Header lines (starting with `||`): The code does
   `strings.ReplaceAll(line, "||", "|")` then `strings.Split(line, "|")`.
   This naively splits on ALL pipe characters, including the `|` inside
   Jira link syntax `[text|url]`.

2. Body rows (starting with `|`): Similarly split on `|` without awareness
   of bracket context. A cell containing `[Google|https://google.com]`
   gets split into two columns: `[Google` and `https://google.com]`.

This produces incorrect column counts, misaligned header/body separators,
and garbled link text in the output.

## Fix approach (depth-aware cell splitter)

Add a new helper function (e.g., `splitTableCells`) that:
  1. Iterates character-by-character through the row string
  2. Tracks `[` / `]` bracket depth (increment on `[`, decrement on `]`)
  3. Only treats `|` (or `||` for headers) as a column separator when
     bracket depth is 0
  4. Returns a slice of cell content strings

Then update both header and body row processing in handleTable() to use
this bracket-aware splitter instead of strings.Split.

Additionally, each parsed cell must have its Jira link syntax converted:
  - `[text|url]` → `[text](url)` (same conversion as handleReferenceLink)
  - This can be done by applying the existing link conversion logic to
    each cell individually before rejoining into the markdown table

## Implementation steps
1. Add `splitTableCells(line string, sep string) []string` to parser.go
2. Update handleTable() to use splitTableCells for both `||` and `|` rows
3. Apply link conversion to each cell before markdown table assembly
4. Ensure header/body column counts stay aligned (pad or trim as needed)
5. Run the failing tests from the table-link test task to verify the fix

## Files to modify
- `pkg/md/jirawiki/parser.go` — handleTable() and new splitTableCells()
- No other files should need changes for this fix

## Key considerations
- The `|` inside `[text|url]` is the ONLY known context where pipes appear
  inside cell content. But be defensive: if future Jira markup introduces
  other `|`-containing constructs, the bracket-depth approach generalizes.
- Edge case: nested brackets `[outer [inner|url] text|url2]` — Jira wiki
  does not support nested links, so single-level bracket tracking suffices.
- Edge case: escaped brackets or pipes — Jira wiki has no escape syntax
  for these, so we don't need to handle backslash escaping.
- Performance: the character-by-character scan is O(n) per row, same
  asymptotic cost as strings.Split. No performance concern.
- This is the HIGHEST PRIORITY fix (p0) because it affects every table
  that contains links — a very common Jira usage pattern.

## Verification
```bash
go test -v -run TestTables ./pkg/md/jirawiki/
```
All 5 new table-link test cases from the test task must pass.

title: Implement underline mark rendering in ADF→MD (Bug 4)
description:
Add underline mark support to the ADF→Markdown translator. Currently,
underline marks in ADF documents are silently dropped because there is no
MarkUnderline constant defined and no rendering logic in the translator.

## Current state
In pkg/adf/adf.go (lines 38-42), the defined mark constants are:
  MarkEm, MarkLink, MarkCode, MarkStrike, MarkStrong

There is NO MarkUnderline constant. The MarkdownTranslator's Open() and
Close() methods (pkg/adf/markdown.go) have switch/case blocks for each
mark type. Since "underline" doesn't match any case, it falls through
silently and the underline formatting is lost.

Test data from existing ADF fixtures includes underline marks, confirming
that Jira Cloud produces ADF documents with this mark type. Users who
underline text in Jira will see that formatting silently vanish when
viewing issues through this CLI.

## Design decision: output format

CommonMark has NO native underline syntax. Options for rendering:

1. **`<u>text</u>`** (recommended) — HTML underline tag. Most terminal
   markdown renderers and GitHub-flavored markdown renderers support inline
   HTML. This is the most semantically accurate representation.

2. **`__text__`** — This is technically "strong emphasis" in CommonMark
   (renders as bold in most renderers). NOT a good choice because it
   would render as bold, not underline.

3. **Plain text with markers** (e.g., `_̈text_̈`) — Non-standard, no
   renderer support. Not viable.

4. **Just render as-is (no markers)** — Current behavior. Loses formatting
   information silently. Not acceptable.

**Recommendation: Use `<u>text</u>`**. It's the standard HTML approach,
widely supported, and semantically correct.

## Implementation steps

1. Add MarkUnderline constant to pkg/adf/adf.go:
   ```go
   MarkUnderline = NodeType("underline")
   ```

2. Add open/close handling in MarkdownTranslator (pkg/adf/markdown.go):
   
   In Open() switch block (around line 145):
   ```go
   case MarkUnderline:
       tag.WriteString(" <u>")
   ```
   
   In Close() switch block (around line 215):
   ```go
   case MarkUnderline:
       tag.WriteString("</u> ")
   ```

3. Update the underline test in adf_test.go to expect `<u>text</u>`
   output instead of the mark-dropped behavior.

## Also check: JiraMarkdownTranslator
The ADF→Jira wiki path (pkg/adf/jiramarkdown.go) via
NewJiraMarkdownTranslator() may also need underline handling. Jira wiki
supports underline with `+text+` syntax. Consider adding:
   Open: tag.WriteString(" +")
   Close: tag.WriteString("+ ")
This is a bonus but should be done in the same change for consistency.

## Files to modify
- `pkg/adf/adf.go` — add MarkUnderline constant (near line 42)
- `pkg/adf/markdown.go` — add underline case to Open() and Close()
- `pkg/adf/jiramarkdown.go` — add underline case (if applicable)
- `pkg/adf/adf_test.go` — update underline test expectation

## Key considerations
- The spacing pattern for marks in markdown.go is: Open adds leading space
  before the marker, Close adds trailing space after. Follow this existing
  convention for underline: ` <u>` open, `</u> ` close.
- The JiraMarkdownTranslator in jiramarkdown.go has its own Open/Close
  methods — check if it also needs underline support with `+text+` syntax.
- Keep the change minimal: just add the constant and the two switch cases.
  No need to refactor the existing mark handling.

## Verification
```bash
go test -v -run TestUnderline ./pkg/adf/
go test -v ./pkg/adf/...
```
The underline fixture test must pass with <u>text</u> output.

title: Fix MD→Wiki unordered list nesting beyond 2 levels
description:
When converting Markdown unordered lists with 3+ levels of nesting to
Jira Wiki format, the third nesting level is flattened to the second
level.

   - Apple

title: Fix typed panel regex to enforce matching open/close tags (Bug 3)
description:
Fix the typed panel regex in pkg/md/md.go so it rejects mismatched
open/close tags (e.g., {info}content{warning}) instead of incorrectly
rewriting them as {panel:bgColor=...} blocks.

## Root cause analysis
In pkg/md/md.go line 25, the typedPanelPattern regex is:

  (?s)\{(info|warning|note|tip|error|success)(?::([^}]*))?\}(.*?)\{(info|warning|note|tip|error|success)\}

This captures the opening type in group 1 and the closing type in group 4,
but it does NOT require them to match. So input like:

  {info}some content{warning}

...matches the regex and gets rewritten to:

  {panel:bgColor=#deebff}some content{panel}

This is incorrect. The opening tag is {info} but the closing tag is
{warning} — these are two different, possibly malformed, unrelated macros.
The converter should leave them unchanged.

## Fix approach

Replace the independent capture groups with a backreference that forces
the closing type to match the opening type. In Go's regexp package
(RE2 syntax), backreferences are NOT supported. So we have two options:

### Option A: Post-match validation (recommended)
Keep the current regex but add a check in convertTypedPanels() that
compares group 1 (open type) with group 4 (close type). If they don't
match, skip the replacement for that match.

Implementation:
```go
func convertTypedPanels(input string) string {
    return typedPanelPattern.ReplaceAllStringFunc(input, func(match string) string {
        groups := typedPanelPattern.FindStringSubmatch(match)
        if groups[1] != groups[4] {
            return match  // Mismatched tags: leave unchanged
        }
        // ... existing rewrite logic using panelColors[groups[1]] ...
    })
}
```

### Option B: Six separate regexes
Create one regex per panel type where the close tag is hardcoded to match:
  `(?s)\{info\}(.*?)\{info\}` etc.
This is more verbose but avoids the mismatch entirely.

**Recommendation**: Option A — minimal code change, easy to understand,
and the match/no-match logic is explicit.

## Implementation steps
1. Modify convertTypedPanels() to use ReplaceAllStringFunc instead of
   ReplaceAllString (or equivalent pattern)
2. Inside the replacement function, compare groups[1] and groups[4]
3. Skip replacement when they don't match
4. Run the mismatched-panel test from the MD→Wiki test task to verify
5. Run ALL existing TestConvertTypedPanels cases to ensure no regressions

## Files to modify
- `pkg/md/md.go` — convertTypedPanels() function (lines 32-57)

## Key considerations
- Go's regexp package uses RE2, which does NOT support backreferences.
  This is why we can't just add \1 in the regex. The post-match validation
  approach is the idiomatic Go solution.
- The existing TestConvertTypedPanels (md_test.go line 111) has 11 test
  cases that must all continue to pass after this change.
- The fix is purely in the convertTypedPanels() helper, which runs before
  the blackfriday renderer. No renderer changes needed.
- Edge case: what about `{info:title=Foo}content{info}` — the title
  attribute is captured in group 2 and does NOT affect the type matching.
  This already works correctly and should continue to work.

## Verification
```bash
go test -v -run TestConvertTypedPanels ./pkg/md/
go test -v -run TestToJiraMD ./pkg/md/
```
The mismatched-tag test must pass. All existing tests must still pass.

title: Add ADF→MD inline node and mark fixture tests
description:
Add 5 targeted, small fixture-based test cases to pkg/adf/adf_test.go that
exercise ADF→Markdown rendering for inline nodes (mention, inlineCard) and
marks (underline, code block language, table cell pipe handling).

## Background & motivation
The ADF→MD path uses MarkdownTranslator (pkg/adf/markdown.go) invoked via
adf.NewMarkdownTranslator(). The existing adf_test.go has only 2 tests:
TestADF (a monolithic golden-string test using testdata/md.json) and
TestADFReplaceAll. There are NO small, targeted fixture tests for specific
node types or marks.

The monolithic test is fragile — any change to any ADF rendering affects
the entire expected output. We need small, isolated fixtures that test one
behavior each. This makes it clear exactly what broke when a test fails.

## Test cases to add (as new test functions in adf_test.go)

1. **Mention node renders display text, account ID omitted**
   Build a minimal ADF document with a single mention node containing
   attrs: {id: "abc123", text: "@John Doe"}.
   Expected output contains "@John Doe" but NOT "abc123".
   Rationale: The plan notes mention rendering is partial — display text
   is rendered but account ID is not. This test documents that as the
   intentional behavior, not a missing feature.

2. **Inline card node renders URL text**
   Build a minimal ADF document with an inlineCard node containing
   attrs: {url: "https://example.com"}.
   Expected output contains the URL.
   Rationale: InlineCard currently renders a pin marker plus URL. This
   test locks down that specific behavior.

3. **Underline mark behavior (document current state)**
   Build a minimal ADF document with a text node carrying an underline
   mark (type: "underline").
   Expected: On current HEAD, the underline mark is silently dropped
   (text appears without any underline rendering). After Bug 4 is fixed,
   expected output should be `<u>text</u>`.
   Rationale: This test will initially document the gap, then serve as
   the passing test after the underline implementation.

4. **Code block preserves language attribute**
   Build a minimal ADF document with a codeBlock node containing
   attrs: {language: "python"} and text content.
   Expected: Fenced code block with ```python language tag.
   Rationale: Language attributes flow through setOpenTagAttributes()
   (markdown.go line 233). This test ensures the attribute pipeline works.

5. **Table cell containing literal pipe character**
   Build a minimal ADF document with a table containing a cell whose
   text includes a literal `|` character.
   Expected: Document the current behavior — either the pipe is escaped
   (good), breaks the table (bad, future fix needed), or is rendered
   as-is (acceptable if Markdown viewers handle it).
   Rationale: This is an intentional "document the behavior" test. The
   plan says: "handled intentionally (escaped or documented as unsupported)".

## File to modify
`pkg/adf/adf_test.go` — add new test functions (do NOT extend the monolithic TestADF)

## Key considerations
- Prefer small, targeted fixtures instead of extending the existing
  monolithic golden string (per plan guidance)
- Build ADF structures programmatically using the adf.ADF, adf.Node,
  adf.NodeValue types — do NOT use JSON files for these small tests
- Test #3 (underline) should initially be written to expect the CURRENT
  behavior (mark dropped), then updated when Bug 4 is implemented
- The adf package imports: check existing test imports and patterns
- Run tests with: go test -v -run TestMention ./pkg/adf/ (etc.)

title: pkg/md/jirawiki: convertReferenceLinks corrupts non-Jira bracket content
description:
Currently, convertReferenceLinks() rewrites any [..] segment, even when it is not Jira wiki link syntax with a pipe separator (parser.go lines ~599-631). For bodies without '|', it emits [](<body>), which corrupts valid markdown links and plain bracket text. This helper is now used in both handleTextEffects() and renderTableCell().

Repro inputs:
1) *[Docs](https://example.com)*
2) ||H||
|[Docs](https://example.com)|

Observed behavior: [Docs](...) becomes [](Docs)(...), producing invalid markdown.
Expected behavior: only convert Jira links that contain an unescaped '|' separator; leave other bracketed content untouched.
